findings.checklist_item: Add a proving command for AC5's close_class/reason clause, e.g. assert every fixture-drift record is closed obsolete with a non-empty reason.
evidence: AC: `rebar search "fixture-drift:" -o json | jq '[.[]|select(.status=="open")]|length'` prints `0`, and each closed record carries `close_class: obsolete` with the reason.
The jq expression filters on status==open only; close_class and reason are never selected or asserted.
findings.finding: AC5's second clause — 'each closed record carries close_class: obsolete with the reason' — has no proving command; the stated jq check only asserts the open-ticket count is 0, leaving the close_class/reason property unverified.
scenarios: A ticket is closed with a different close_class (or the reason string omitted) — open count is still 0, so the AC's command passes while its prose is violated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: `rebar search "fixture-drift:" -o json | jq -e 'all(.[]; .status=="closed" and .close_class=="obsolete" and (.close_reason|length>0))'` (adjust field names to the tracker schema).

findings.checklist_item: Resolve the DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH release-note bullet: cite the upstream story/commit that performed the removal (as done for the evals extra), or drop/rescope the bullet to match 'No source files'.
evidence: Release note: 'plan_replay.ledger.DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH removed, ledger defaults resolving at call time'
Scope: 'No source files, and nothing under `evals/`.'
The evals-registration claim is cited to sibling story d279; the DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH removal has no equivalent provenance.
findings.finding: The release note bullet 'plan_replay.ledger.DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH removed, ledger defaults resolving at call time' asserts a source-code change, yet Scope states 'No source files' and the plan supplies no cite that this removal happened upstream (unlike the evals registration, which is explicitly attributed to d279).
scenarios: Implementer reads the release note, concludes they must remove DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH, but Scope forbids source edits — two directions.
Reviewer/consumer reads a release note describing a removal that never occurred in any shipped change.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the disposition mechanism with tracker reality: the 71 fixture-drift tickets are already closed (close_class=obsolete) per this ticket's own 2026-09-08 comment — re-scope the Approach to state the batch is already applied (or re-verify-only) rather than presenting the open->closed transition loop as live remaining work.
evidence: Ticket 00b4-b253-3052-4181: status=closed, close_class='obsolete'
Story ticket comment: 'Bulk-closed 71 generated fixture-drift: task tickets on 2026-09-08 ... no producer/consumer remains on main.'

Plan Testing section concedes: 're-running the disposition batch is a no-op, each ticket already closed, so exit 10 is expected and skipped' — contradicting the Approach's presentation of the loop as the live mechanism
findings.finding: The disposition mechanism in Approach ('for each id from search(title:fixture-drift: status:open), transition_ticket(id, "open", "closed", ...)') cannot achieve its goal: the 71 fixture-drift tickets are ALREADY closed with close_class=obsolete. Spot-checked 00b4-b253-3052-4181 shows status=closed, close_class=obsolete, and the story ticket's own comment records 'Bulk-closed 71 generated fixture-drift: task tickets on 2026-09-08'. The search for status:open will return zero rows, so the transition loop transitions nothing — the named deliverable is already satisfied upstream.
scenarios: Implementer runs the search, gets 0 open tickets, transitions nothing, and the AC5 'prints 0' passes for a reason unrelated to this story's work
Completion verifier is asked to confirm a transition batch that this ticket already performed weeks earlier
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the transition-loop instruction with a verify-only step that asserts `rebar search "fixture-drift:" ... status==open length == 0` and confirms each record already carries close_class=obsolete, and note in Approach that the bulk close already landed under this ticket on 2026-09-08.

findings.checklist_item: Align AC5's 'the reason' with the reason actually recorded on the already-closed tickets (the ADR-0113 self-heal-loop wording), or drop the specific-string requirement, since the records are already closed and their reason cannot be retroactively changed to the plan's proposed text.
evidence: Applied close_reason on 00b4-b253-3052-4181: 'fixture-drift ticket mooted by ADR 0113 self-heal loop; no producer/consumer remains (see bumpy-slight-bobwhite)'
Plan-proposed reason: 'superseded by the scheduled fixture-heal loop (rebar criteria heal, heal.py), which re-mines every criterion on fixture_heal.interval_days ...'
findings.finding: AC5 and the Approach propose a specific long close reason ('superseded by the scheduled fixture-heal loop ... per-entry drift tickets have no producer and no consumer'), but the already-closed records carry a DIFFERENT reason ('fixture-drift ticket mooted by ADR 0113 self-heal loop; no producer/consumer remains (see bumpy-slight-bobwhite)'). AC5 ('each closed record carries close_class: obsolete with the reason') is therefore either already-satisfied-with-a-different-string or unsatisfiable without re-closing immutable closed records.
